title: Empty a urinary drainage bag into a graduate, spout never touching it, then close the valve and clip the tube back
instruction: Empty the drainage bag into the graduate without letting the drain spout touch the graduate, then close the drain and put the tube back in its holder.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00; 1,505,900 US jobs, 2025): "Measure and record food and liquid intake or urinary and fecal output, reporting changes to medical or nursing staff." LPNs (29-2061.00; 666,900): "Record food and fluid intake and output." For a patient with a Foley catheter this means emptying the drainage bag into a graduate, at least every shift or when half full; 15-25 % of hospital patients get one (CDC). It is a graded nurse-aide exam skill (Arizona checklist): barrier under the bag, graduate on it, open the drain, empty it completely, "Avoids touching the graduate with any part of the tubing", close the drain, put it back in its holder. CDC's CAUTI guideline (III.B.3): a clean container per patient, no splashing, the spigot never touching it. The difficulty is physical: one hand holds a spout on soft tubing 5 cm over an 11 cm mouth and follows the stream as its arc shortens, the other twists the valve.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table top (the floor beside the bed). Catheter bag floor holder (500 mm tall, 210 mm deep, steel), its base fixed at x 45, y -4; hook 48 cm up at x 42. Bard 154002 2000 mL urinary drainage bag hanging on it by its hanger, front toward the robot: 18 cm wide, 4.5 cm thick, 25 cm tall (modeled), bottom 21 cm up, holding 600 mL of clear tap water standing in for urine (in the sim and the real trial: hygienic and the same every trial; it drains like urine). Its drain tube (9 mm, clear PVC) leaves the bottom's middle, runs out 8 cm toward the robot and folds up 11 cm in front of the bag; the 22 mm blue twist-valve collar at its end sits closed in the holder clip, on a holder tab out from the bag's front, the spout end pointing up at x 34, y -4, 34 cm up. Medline 1000 mL graduated triangular container (modeled round, 11.2 cm across the mouth inside, 13.5 cm deep inside, 90 g), empty, standing at x 23, y -24.5 beside the underpad, its handle toward the robot's right. A blue absorbent underpad (30 x 40 cm) lies flat on the floor under the bag's front centered at x 30, y 2. The layout is fixed (object_jitter=0).
scoring: In the graduate is the water that reached it; spilled is what landed anywhere else (underpad, table). A touch is the spout (the valve collar and the last 2 cm of tube) within 1 mm of the graduate's wall, rim or floor at any time. Score 0 when more than 20 mL is spilled (a puddle on the floor). Otherwise: 1.0 for at least 570 mL in the graduate (95 % of the 600 mL), at most 5 mL spilled, the valve closed (within 10 degrees of its closed stop), the tube back in its clip, the graduate upright (within 10 degrees of vertical) and both hands clear (every tool point and pad tip 1 cm from the spout, the tube and the graduate) with everything still, held 1 s; 0.75 for at least 570 mL with the valve closed and the graduate upright; 0.5 for at least 570 mL otherwise (valve left open, graduate tipped after) or at least 300 mL with the valve closed and the graduate upright; 0.25 for at least 100 mL. A touch at any time caps the trial at 0.25. Doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Real trial: the graduate's net mass on a 1 g kitchen scale (1 g = 1 mL); spilled is the pre-weighed underpad's gain plus any wiped up off the table; a touch is any blue transferred from the washable-marker band on the graduate's rim to a white tissue wiped over the spout; valve, clip, graduate upright and hands clear from the photo and video.
reset_notes: About 4 minutes. Unhook the bag and drain what is left into the sink; weigh 600 g of clear tap water into the graduate on the scale and pour it through a small kitchen funnel into the bag's inlet tube held above the bag; rehang the bag on the hook, close the valve and push the spout into the holder clip. Empty, dry and tare the graduate, renew the washable-marker band on its rim, set it on its tape circle with the handle to the right, and lay a fresh pre-weighed underpad on its tape marks.
fidelity: Clear tap water in sim and real trial (drains like urine). Lumped flow model (as in our IV-hub task): the pillow bag drains through the spout as an orifice (Torricelli, Cd 0.61, 6 mm bore, real head, times the valve's opening); the stream follows its arc into the mouth or onto the floor; the graduate holds the volume, shows its level and spills if tipped. No splashing. Rigid bag on a hook hinge, mass fixed at full; the tube is two hinged links; clip and valve are click laws. Graduate round.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 (1,899 steps / 95.0 s; 600 mL in the graduate, 0 mL spilled, no touch, valve closed, tube clipped). Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps). Both on task.py 1ef5af9c2b33.
